native_result.query: Does increased time preference leads to higher BMI?
native_result.HypoA: Higher time preference associated with higher BMI for 1989 data.
native_result.WorkflowA:
1. Selected appropriate variables from the raw data
e.g.: Height: Height of respondent on 1985 instead of 1981.
      Income: Total net family income, 1989 (There are many other income variables in the raw data)
      Age:    Age of respondent at 1989 (Derived from Age at 1979).
Data Transformation:
2. Replaced -1 to -5 values (unavailable data) with NaN
3. Imputed the missing values in the AGE and INCOME variable with mean.
4. AGE_1989 had missing values, hence derived the variable as [AGE_1979 + 10]
5. Created a BMI variable using: bmi = (weight) * 0.453592 / (height) * 0.0254
6. Divided the Family income variable by 1000$ (Mentioned in the paper)
7. Created an AGE^2 variable (From the paper)
8. One-hot encoded RACE variable into BLACK and HISPANIC
9. One-hot encooded GENDER variable into MALE and FEMALE
10. Selected 'Was more money put into or taken out of R/spouse savings since last interview, 1989' as the Time Preference variable.
  DISSAVED = 1 if 'TOOK MORE MONEY OUT' else 0
  SAMESAVE = 1 if 'NO SAVINGS' or 'NO CHANGE' else 0
11. Dropped the unimportant columns for replication
12. DISSAVED and SAMESAVE as independent variables and BMI as dependent variable
13. Fit an OLS Regression Model
native_result.HypoB: En la cohorte NLSY79, mayor preferencia temporal — aproximada por menor patrimonio familiar neto acumulado en 1996 — está asociada a mayor IMC tanto en 1989 como en 1992. Coeficiente principal (BMI92, controles completos): β = -0.744 unidades de IMC por unidad de log(wealth96), EE HC1 = 0.412, p = 0.071, N = 4259; bajo MICE m=20 se mantiene negativo y significativo (β pooled = -0.542, p = 0.033). Triangulación con savings-1989 muestra mediana de BMI92 monotónicamente creciente desde PUT IN (24.79) hasta NO SAVINGS (25.75), con dummies significativas. Asociación más fuerte en mujeres (interacción wealth × female = -2.67, p < 0.001).
native_result.WorkflowB: Cargar data/nls_raw.csv; convertir pesos de libras a kg y altura 1985 de pulgadas a metros para construir BMI89 y BMI92 con denominador único de altura; transformar Family net wealth 1996 con log(wealth - min + 1) para manejar negativos; winsorizar al 1 %/99 %; ajustar OLS con errores HC1 en jerarquía de tres niveles sobre ambos outcomes; triangular con las dummies de savings-1989 (ref PUT IN); estimar interacción log(wealth96) × female; calcular VIF; y validar la conclusión principal con MICE m=20 con regresión estocástica encadenada y pooling de Rubin.

sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) respondents analyzed for 1989, using height measured in 1985.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Higher time preference associated with higher BMI for 1989 data.

sub_hypo.text: In the NLSY79 cohort, greater time preference, proxied by lower accumulated family net wealth in 1996, is associated with higher BMI in both 1989 and 1992.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 participants; BMI measured in 1989 and 1992 and family net wealth measured in 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Negative association between log-transformed wealth and both BMI outcomes. BMI uses weights converted from pounds to kilograms and the same 1985 height converted to meters; wealth is transformed as log(wealth - min + 1), with 1st/99th-percentile winsorization in the workflow. OLS uses three hierarchical adjustment levels and HC1 errors. For BMI92 with full controls: β = -0.744, HC1 SE = 0.412, p = 0.071, N = 4259. MICE with 20 imputations and Rubin pooling retains a negative, significant association: pooled β = -0.542, p = 0.033. Specific control variables are not provided.

sub_hypo.text: In the NLSY79 cohort, median BMI in 1992 increases monotonically across 1989 savings categories from putting more money in to having no savings.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 participants with savings behavior measured in 1989 and BMI measured in 1992.
variables: Was more money put into or taken out of R/spouse savings since last interview, 1989
sub_hypo.relations: Median BMI92 increases monotonically from PUT IN (24.79) to NO SAVINGS (25.75). Savings-category dummy associations are reported as significant, with PUT IN as the reference category.

sub_hypo.text: In the NLSY79 cohort, the negative association between family net wealth in 1996 and BMI is stronger among women.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 participants, comparing women with men.
sub_hypo.relations: Sex moderates the wealth–BMI association: the log(wealth96) × female interaction is negative (β = -2.67, p < 0.001), indicating a stronger negative association among women. The specific BMI year for this reported interaction coefficient is not stated.
